### `heading-hierarchy` {#heading-hierarchy}

Warns when a heading skips a level, such as `# Methods` followed by
`### Results`. Use consecutive levels to make the document's structure clear.

The fix lowers the skipped heading to the next level after the preceding
heading. Review the surrounding sections if the heading belongs elsewhere.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                      | Severity |
  | ----------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`heading-hierarchy`](#heading-hierarchy) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
# Methods

### Results
```

```text
warning: [heading-hierarchy] Heading level skipped from h1 to h3; expected h2
 --> example.qmd:3:1
  |
1 | # Methods
  | - previous heading is here
2 |
3 | ### Results
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Change heading level from 3 to 2
```

After `panache lint --fix`:

```markdown
# Methods

## Results
```

### `empty-list-item` {#empty-list-item}

Warns about list items with no text. Fill in the missing item or remove it.

A bare `-` directly below text can also turn the preceding line into a heading
instead of creating an empty item. The rule warns about that form too.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                  | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`empty-list-item`](#empty-list-item) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
- First item
-
- Last item
```

```text
warning: [empty-list-item] List item has no content
 --> example.qmd:2:1
  |
2 | -
  | ^
```

### `empty-values` {#empty-values}

Warns about YAML keys with nothing after the colon, such as `title:`. YAML
treats these values as null, which may indicate an unfinished setting.

Supply a value, remove the key, or write `null` or `~` if null is intentional.
The rule checks frontmatter and code-cell options, but not mappings written
inside braces, such as `{title: }`.

The optional fix removes the whole key. It requires `--unsafe-fixes` because
removing a setting can change the document's behavior.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                            | Severity |
  | ------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`empty-values`](#empty-values) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
---
title:
---
```

```text
warning: [empty-values] Key `title` has an empty value (implicit null)
 --> example.qmd:2:1
  |
2 | title:
  | ^^^^^
  = help: Remove the empty key `title`
  = help: Provide a value, remove the key, or write an explicit `null` if the empty value is intentional
```

After `panache lint --fix --unsafe-fixes` (review the change before applying
it):

```markdown
---
---
```

### `consumer-divergence` {#consumer-divergence}

Warns about YAML values that Quarto and Pandoc read differently. For example,
Pandoc reads `no` as false, while Quarto reads it as the string `"no"`.
Leading-zero values such as `0755` can also have different meanings.

Quote a value if you mean a string. Otherwise, write `true`, `false`, or a
decimal integer explicitly. This check applies to Quarto frontmatter, where both
YAML versions are used.

The optional fix quotes the value. It requires `--unsafe-fixes` because the
author may have intended a boolean or number instead of a string.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Requirements
:   The Quarto flavor.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                          | Severity |
  | --------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`consumer-divergence`](#consumer-divergence) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
---
country: no
---
```

```text
warning: [consumer-divergence] Key `country`: value `no` is the boolean `false` to pandoc (YAML 1.1) but the string `"no"` to Quarto's js-yaml (1.2)
 --> example.qmd:2:10
  |
2 | country: no
  |          ^^
  = help: Quote the value as `'no'`
  = help: Quote the value to force a string under every consumer, or write the explicit `true`/`false` (or canonical integer) you mean
```

After `panache lint --fix --unsafe-fixes` (review the change before applying
it):

```markdown
---
country: 'no'
---
```

### `math-syntax` {#math-syntax}

Reports unbalanced braces, unmatched environments, and other structural errors
inside TeX math. These errors can prevent PDF output or leave an equation
missing from HTML output.

Check the indicated delimiter and add, remove, or correct its partner. The rule
checks structure, not command names or mathematical meaning. If a TeX macro
deliberately supplies a delimiter elsewhere, suppress this rule for that
passage.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   At least one `tex-math-*` extension is enabled.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                          | Severity |
  | ---                                                           | ---      |
  | [`math-unclosed-group`](#math-unclosed-group)                 | Error    |
  | [`math-unexpected-close-brace`](#math-unexpected-close-brace) | Error    |
  | [`math-unclosed-environment`](#math-unclosed-environment)     | Error    |
  | [`math-mismatched-environment`](#math-mismatched-environment) | Error    |
  | [`math-unexpected-end`](#math-unexpected-end)                 | Error    |
  | [`math-unclosed-delimiter`](#math-unclosed-delimiter)         | Error    |
  | [`math-unexpected-right`](#math-unexpected-right)             | Error    |
  | [`math-unexpected-dollar`](#math-unexpected-dollar)           | Error    |

#### `math-unclosed-group` {#math-unclosed-group}

An opening `{` has no matching `}`.

#### `math-unexpected-close-brace` {#math-unexpected-close-brace}

A closing `}` has no matching `{`.

#### `math-unclosed-environment` {#math-unclosed-environment}

A `\begin{...}` has no matching `\end{...}`.

#### `math-mismatched-environment` {#math-mismatched-environment}

The name in `\end{...}` differs from the open environment.

#### `math-unexpected-end` {#math-unexpected-end}

A `\end{...}` has no matching `\begin{...}`.

#### `math-unclosed-delimiter` {#math-unclosed-delimiter}

A `\left` has no matching `\right`.

#### `math-unexpected-right` {#math-unexpected-right}

A `\right` has no matching `\left`.

#### `math-unexpected-dollar` {#math-unexpected-dollar}

An unescaped `$` appears inside TeX math. Use `\$` for a literal dollar sign.

#### Examples

A group is missing its closing brace:

```markdown
$\frac{1}{2$
```

```text
error: [math-unclosed-group] unclosed `{` group
 --> example.qmd:1:10
  |
1 | $\frac{1}{2$
  |          ^
```

A closing brace has no matching opener:

```markdown
$a}b$
```

```text
error: [math-unexpected-close-brace] unmatched closing brace `}`
 --> example.qmd:1:3
  |
1 | $a}b$
  |   ^
```

An environment is missing its end:

```markdown
$$
\begin{aligned} x &= 1
$$
```

```text
error: [math-unclosed-environment] `\begin` without a matching `\end`
 --> example.qmd:2:1
  |
2 | \begin{aligned} x &= 1
  | ^^^^^^
```

The environment names do not match:

```markdown
$$\begin{aligned}x\end{matrix}$$
```

```text
error: [math-mismatched-environment] `\end` name does not match the open `\begin`
 --> example.qmd:1:23
  |
1 | $$\begin{aligned}x\end{matrix}$$
  |                       ^^^^^^^^
```

An environment ends without being opened:

```markdown
$x \end{aligned}$
```

```text
error: [math-unexpected-end] `\end` without a matching `\begin`
 --> example.qmd:1:4
  |
1 | $x \end{aligned}$
  |    ^^^^
```

A scalable delimiter is missing its partner:

```markdown
$\left(x$
```

```text
error: [math-unclosed-delimiter] `\left` without a matching `\right`
 --> example.qmd:1:2
  |
1 | $\left(x$
  |  ^^^^^
```

A closing scalable delimiter has no opener:

```markdown
$x\right)$
```

```text
error: [math-unexpected-right] `\right` without a matching `\left`
 --> example.qmd:1:3
  |
1 | $x\right)$
  |   ^^^^^^
```

A dollar sign appears inside display math:

```markdown
$$
$ a
$$
```

```text
error: [math-unexpected-dollar] unescaped `$` inside TeX math ends math mode
 --> example.qmd:2:1
  |
2 | $ a
  | ^
```

### `inline-math-line-break` {#inline-math-line-break}

Warns about `\\` at the top level of inline math. It means a row break, so
`\\mathrm{x}` does not mean `\mathrm{x}`.

Remove the extra backslash if you meant a command. If you need several rows, use
display math with a suitable environment. Row breaks inside constructs such as
`matrix`, `array`, and `\substack` are allowed.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   At least one `tex-math-*` extension is enabled.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                | Severity |
  | --------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`inline-math-line-break`](#inline-math-line-break) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
$\\mathrm{x}$
```

```text
warning: [inline-math-line-break] top-level `\\` is not portable in inline math
 --> example.qmd:1:2
  |
1 | $\\mathrm{x}$
  |  ^^
  = help: `\\mathrm` is parsed as a line break followed by `mathrm`; use `\mathrm` if you intended a command
```

### `heading-eaten-attrs` {#heading-eaten-attrs}

Warns when an HTML comment after a heading's attributes prevents Pandoc from
recognizing them. The attributes then appear as text, and links to the intended
heading ID may stop working.

Move the comment to its own line. A heading's `{#id .class}` block must be
followed only by whitespace.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.header-attributes = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                          | Severity |
  | --------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`heading-eaten-attrs`](#heading-eaten-attrs) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
# Results {#results} <!-- Draft -->
```

```text
warning: [heading-eaten-attrs] Comment on a heading line with `{...}` attributes; pandoc treats the brace block as literal text when anything follows it on the line.
 --> example.qmd:1:22
  |
1 | # Results {#results} <!-- Draft -->
  |                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Move the comment to its own line before or after the heading.
```

### `heading-strip-comments-residue` {#heading-strip-comments-residue}

Warns about comments on a heading line that also contains attributes. Running
`pandoc --strip-comments` removes the comment but leaves its surrounding spaces.

Move the comment to a separate line. Enable this rule if your publishing process
uses `--strip-comments`.

Default
:   Off

Enable this rule with
`[lint] extend-select = ["heading-strip-comments-residue"]`.

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.header-attributes = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                                | Severity |
  | ---                                                                 | ---      |
  | [`heading-strip-comments-residue`](#heading-strip-comments-residue) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
# Results <!-- Draft --> {#results}
```

```text
warning: [heading-strip-comments-residue] Comment on a heading line adjacent to `{...}` attributes; `pandoc --strip-comments` will leave stray whitespace on the heading.
 --> example.qmd:1:11
  |
1 | # Results <!-- Draft --> {#results}
  |           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Move the comment to its own line before or after the heading.
```

### `adjacent-footnote-refs` {#adjacent-footnote-refs}

Warns when footnote references touch, as in `[^a][^b]`. Their superscript
numbers can run together: footnotes 7 and 8 may look like footnote 78.

The fix inserts a space between the references so readers can distinguish them.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Requirements
:   `extensions.footnotes = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                | Severity |
  | --------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`adjacent-footnote-refs`](#adjacent-footnote-refs) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
Text[^a][^b].

[^a]: First note.

[^b]: Second note.
```

```text
warning: [adjacent-footnote-refs] Adjacent footnote references render as a single superscript number; insert a space to keep them visually distinct
 --> example.qmd:1:9
  |
1 | Text[^a][^b].
  |         ^^^^
  = help: Insert a space between the footnote references
```

After `panache lint --fix`:

```markdown
Text[^a] [^b].

[^a]: First note.

[^b]: Second note.
```

### `blank-line-in-display-math` {#blank-line-in-display-math}

Warns when a blank line separates apparent `$$` math delimiters. Pandoc ends the
paragraph at the blank line, so the equation may appear as ordinary text.

Remove the blank line if the lines belong to one equation. Use separate,
complete math blocks if you intended two equations.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.tex-math-dollars = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                        | Severity |
  | ---                                                         | ---      |
  | [`blank-line-in-display-math`](#blank-line-in-display-math) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
$$
x = 1

$$
```

```text
warning: [blank-line-in-display-math] Blank line ends the paragraph before this display-math delimiter closes, so pandoc renders both `$$` markers as literal text
 --> example.qmd:1:1
  |
1 | $$
  | ^^
```

### `blank-line-in-inline-footnote` {#blank-line-in-inline-footnote}

Warns when an apparent inline footnote crosses a blank line. Inline footnotes
can wrap over ordinary line breaks, but they cannot contain several paragraphs.
The `^[` and `]` markers may appear literally in the output.

Remove the blank line, or use a reference-style footnote if the note needs
several paragraphs.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.inline-footnotes = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                              | Severity |
  | ---                                                               | ---      |
  | [`blank-line-in-inline-footnote`](#blank-line-in-inline-footnote) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
Text^[A note

continued here].
```

```text
warning: [blank-line-in-inline-footnote] Blank line ends the paragraph before this inline footnote closes, so pandoc renders the footnote markers as literal text
 --> example.qmd:1:5
  |
1 | Text^[A note
  |     ^^
```

### `footnote-ref-in-footnote-def` {#footnote-ref-in-footnote-def}

Warns about a footnote reference inside another footnote's definition. Pandoc
does not nest these notes, so the inner reference appears as literal text
instead of linking to a note.

Include the explanation directly in the outer note, move the reference into the
main text, or remove it.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.footnotes = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                            | Severity |
  | ---                                                             | ---      |
  | [`footnote-ref-in-footnote-def`](#footnote-ref-in-footnote-def) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
Text[^a].

[^a]: See [^b].

[^b]: More detail.
```

```text
warning: [footnote-ref-in-footnote-def] Footnote reference '[^b]' inside a footnote definition body is silently dropped by pandoc (rendered as literal text)
 --> example.qmd:3:11
  |
3 | [^a]: See [^b].
  |           ^^^^
  = help: footnotes do not nest in pandoc; inline the prose, restructure to keep the reference outside the definition body, or remove it
```

### `duplicate-reference-labels` {#duplicate-reference-labels}

Warns when reference links, footnotes, or cross-references reuse a label. Give
each definition a unique label, and update any references to it.

Reference-link and footnote labels are also checked across files that are
combined into one document, such as Quarto includes and bookdown chapters.
Independently rendered Quarto documents may reuse those labels. Cross-reference
labels, such as figure IDs, are checked across the project.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                        | Severity |
  | ---                                                         | ---      |
  | [`duplicate-reference-labels`](#duplicate-reference-labels) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
[Read more][guide].

[guide]: /first
[guide]: /second
```

```text
warning: [duplicate-reference-labels] Duplicate reference label '[guide]' (first defined at line 3)
 --> example.qmd:4:1
  |
4 | [guide]: /second
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

### `undefined-references` {#undefined-references}

Warns about reference links and footnotes whose labels have no definition. Add
the missing definition or correct the label. This includes shortcut links such
as `[guide]` and collapsed links such as `[guide][]`.

Labels include their inline markup: `[<span>Guide</span>]` does not match a
definition named `[Guide]`.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                      | Severity |
  | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`undefined-reference-label`](#undefined-reference-label) | Warning  |
  | [`undefined-footnote-id`](#undefined-footnote-id)         | Warning  |

#### `undefined-reference-label` {#undefined-reference-label}

A reference-style link has no matching definition.

#### `undefined-footnote-id` {#undefined-footnote-id}

A footnote reference has no matching definition.

#### Examples

```markdown
[Read more][missing].
```

```text
warning: [undefined-reference-label] Reference label '[missing]' not found
 --> example.qmd:1:13
  |
1 | [Read more][missing].
  |             ^^^^^^^
```

```markdown
Text[^missing].
```

```text
warning: [undefined-footnote-id] Footnote '[^missing]' not found
 --> example.qmd:1:5
  |
1 | Text[^missing].
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^
```

### `undefined-anchor` {#undefined-anchor}

Warns about links such as `[Methods](#methods)` when the destination ID does not
exist. Correct the link, add an explicit `{#methods}` ID, or link to an existing
heading. IDs are case-sensitive.

The rule recognizes generated heading IDs, explicit attributes, code-cell
labels, and supported HTML IDs. In Quarto and bookdown projects, it also checks
anchors in other project documents and their includes.

Links to another file, full URLs, and bare `#` links are excluded. With
citations enabled, `#ref-key` can resolve to a bibliography entry when the
document cites that key.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                    | Severity |
  | --------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`undefined-anchor`](#undefined-anchor) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
[Methods](#methods)
```

```text
warning: [undefined-anchor] Anchor '#methods' not found in document
 --> example.qmd:1:12
  |
1 | [Methods](#methods)
  |            ^^^^^^^
```

### `unused-definitions` {#unused-definitions}

Warns about reference-link and footnote definitions that are never used. Remove
an obsolete definition, or add the reference that was meant to use it.

During project linting, references in other project documents are included when
checking whether a definition is used.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                  | Severity |
  | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`unused-definition-label`](#unused-definition-label) | Warning  |
  | [`unused-footnote-id`](#unused-footnote-id)           | Warning  |

#### `unused-definition-label` {#unused-definition-label}

A reference-link definition is never used.

#### `unused-footnote-id` {#unused-footnote-id}

A footnote definition is never used.

#### Examples

```markdown
[unused]: https://example.com
```

```text
warning: [unused-definition-label] Reference definition '[unused]' is never used
 --> example.qmd:1:1
  |
1 | [unused]: https://example.com
  | ^^^^^^^^
```

```markdown
[^unused]: A note.
```

```text
warning: [unused-footnote-id] Footnote '[^unused]' is never used
 --> example.qmd:1:1
  |
1 | [^unused]: A note.
  | ^^^^^^^^^
```

### `unspaced-citation` {#unspaced-citation}

Warns when a known citation key touches the preceding word, as in
`See@smith2024`. Pandoc treats that form as ordinary text.

Insert a space (`See @smith2024`) or use a bracketed citation
(`See[@smith2024]`). The rule checks only keys found in a bibliography or inline
`references:` entry, so ordinary email addresses are left alone. Escape a
literal at sign as `\@` if it should not introduce a citation.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.citations = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                      | Severity |
  | ----------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`unspaced-citation`](#unspaced-citation) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
---
references:
  - id: smith2024
    title: A study
---

See@smith2024.
```

```text
warning: [unspaced-citation] Citation '@smith2024' is glued to the preceding text and will not be recognized; separate it with a space or wrap it in brackets '[@smith2024]'
 --> example.qmd:7:4
  |
7 | See@smith2024.
  |    ^^^^^^^^^^
```

### `malformed-citation` {#malformed-citation}

Warns about incomplete citation markers, such as `[@]`, `[@ key]`, an empty
`@{}`, or a missing closing bracket. Write a key immediately after `@`, and
close every bracket or brace. Use `@{...}` for keys with unusual characters.

The rule skips code, math, escaped markers, email addresses, and working links.
To check whether a complete key exists in the bibliography, use
[`citation-keys`](#citation-keys).

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.citations = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                        | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`malformed-citation`](#malformed-citation) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
See [@].
```

```text
warning: [malformed-citation] Citation marker has no key; add a citation key after '@'
 --> example.qmd:1:6
  |
1 | See [@].
  |      ^
```

### `duplicate-yaml-anchor` {#duplicate-yaml-anchor}

Warns when a YAML document defines the same `&name` anchor more than once. An
alias may then refer to a different value than you intended.

Rename the duplicate anchor and its aliases, or remove the extra definition.
Anchors in separate frontmatter or code-cell option blocks are independent.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                              | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`duplicate-yaml-anchor`](#duplicate-yaml-anchor) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
---
first: &value 1
second: &value 2
---
```

```text
warning: [duplicate-yaml-anchor] YAML anchor `&value` is defined more than once
 --> example.qmd:3:9
  |
3 | second: &value 2
  |         ^^^^^^
```

### `unused-yaml-anchor` {#unused-yaml-anchor}

Warns about a YAML `&name` anchor with no matching `*name` alias in the same
YAML document. Remove the anchor if it is no longer needed, or use an alias
where you meant to reuse the value.

Aliases in another frontmatter or code-cell option block do not count as uses of
the anchor.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                        | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`unused-yaml-anchor`](#unused-yaml-anchor) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
---
title: &title A report
---
```

```text
warning: [unused-yaml-anchor] YAML anchor `&title` is never used
 --> example.qmd:2:8
  |
2 | title: &title A report
  |        ^^^^^^
```

### `citation-keys` {#citation-keys}

Checks cited keys against bibliography files and inline `references:` entries.
It also reports files that cannot be read or parsed, duplicate bibliography
keys, and duplicate inline reference IDs.

Check the file path and bibliography syntax first. Then correct missing keys or
give conflicting entries distinct IDs.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.citations = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                              | Severity |
  | ---                                                               | ---      |
  | [`bibliography-load-error`](#bibliography-load-error)             | Error    |
  | [`bibliography-parse-error`](#bibliography-parse-error)           | Error    |
  | [`missing-bibliography-key`](#missing-bibliography-key)           | Warning  |
  | [`duplicate-bibliography-key`](#duplicate-bibliography-key)       | Warning  |
  | [`duplicate-inline-reference-id`](#duplicate-inline-reference-id) | Warning  |

#### `bibliography-load-error` {#bibliography-load-error}

A bibliography file could not be read. Check that the path is correct and the
file is accessible.

#### `bibliography-parse-error` {#bibliography-parse-error}

A bibliography file contains invalid syntax. Correct it using the syntax for its
file format.

#### `missing-bibliography-key` {#missing-bibliography-key}

A cited key is absent from the loaded bibliography and inline references.

#### `duplicate-bibliography-key` {#duplicate-bibliography-key}

More than one bibliography entry uses the same key. Rename or remove the
duplicate.

#### `duplicate-inline-reference-id` {#duplicate-inline-reference-id}

An inline reference ID is repeated, or conflicts with a key in a bibliography
file.

#### Examples

The declared bibliography file does not exist:

```markdown
---
bibliography: missing.bib
---
```

```text
error: [bibliography-load-error] Failed to load bibliography missing.bib: File not found
 --> example.qmd:2:15
  |
2 | bibliography: missing.bib
  |               ^^^^^^^^^^^
```

The bibliography file cannot be parsed:

With `refs.json`:

```json
not valid JSON
```

```markdown
---
bibliography: refs.json
---
```

```text
error: [bibliography-parse-error] Invalid bibliography entry: Invalid CSL-JSON: expected ident at line 1 column 2
 --> example.qmd:1:1
  |
1 | / ---
2 | | bibliography: refs.json
3 | | ---
  | |____^
```

A citation has no matching entry:

With `refs.bib`:

```bibtex
@book{known, title = {A Book}}
```

```markdown
---
bibliography: refs.bib
---

See [@missing].
```

```text
warning: [missing-bibliography-key] Citation key 'missing' not found in bibliography
 --> example.qmd:5:6
  |
5 | See [@missing].
  |      ^^^^^^^^
```

Two bibliography entries share a key:

With `refs.bib`:

```bibtex
@book{same, title = {First}}
@book{same, title = {Second}}
```

```markdown
---
bibliography: refs.bib
---
```

```text
warning: [duplicate-bibliography-key] Duplicate bibliography key 'same' in refs.bib and refs.bib
 --> example.qmd:2:15
  |
2 | bibliography: refs.bib
  |               ^^^^^^^^
```

Two inline references share an ID:

```markdown
---
references:
  - id: same
    title: First
  - id: same
    title: Second
---
```

```text
warning: [duplicate-inline-reference-id] Duplicate inline reference id 'same'
 --> example.qmd:5:9
  |
5 |   - id: same
  |         ^^^^
```

### `citation-nonbreaking-space` {#citation-nonbreaking-space}

Warns about a breakable space before a bracketed citation. Line wrapping can
leave the citation at the start of a line, separated from the text it supports.

The fix replaces the gap with Pandoc's nonbreaking space escape, `\ `. If that
escape is disabled, it inserts a nonbreaking space character instead. Citations
at the start of a paragraph, after a hard line break, or already preceded by a
nonbreaking space are left alone.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Requirements
:   `extensions.citations = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                        | Severity |
  | ---                                                         | ---      |
  | [`citation-nonbreaking-space`](#citation-nonbreaking-space) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
A result [@smith2024].
```

```text
warning: [citation-nonbreaking-space] Breakable space before citation; the rendered citation can be stranded at the start of a line
 --> example.qmd:1:9
  |
1 | A result [@smith2024].
  |         ^
  = help: Replace with a non-breaking space (`\ `)
```

After `panache lint --fix`:

```markdown
A result\ [@smith2024].
```

### `crossref-as-link-target` {#crossref-as-link-target}

Warns about link destinations beginning with `@`, such as `[Figure 2](@fig-2)`.
That creates a link to the literal URL `@fig-2`.

Use `@fig-2` on its own for a cross-reference, or `[Figure 2](#fig-2)` for a
link to an ID. The fix changes the destination's leading `@` to `#`.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Requirements
:   `extensions.citations = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                  | Severity |
  | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`crossref-as-link-target`](#crossref-as-link-target) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
# Results {#results}

[Results](@results)
```

```text
warning: [crossref-as-link-target] Link target starts with '@'; cross-references and citation keys must stand alone, not appear as a link destination
 --> example.qmd:3:11
  |
3 | [Results](@results)
  |           ^
  = help: Replace '@' with '#' to link to an anchor
```

After `panache lint --fix`:

```markdown
# Results {#results}

[Results](#results)
```

### `chunk-label-spaces` {#chunk-label-spaces}

Warns about spaces in executable code-cell labels. Labels such as
`several words` can be difficult to reference reliably.

Use a label such as `several-words` or `several_words`, and update references to
the cell.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.fenced-code-attributes = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                        | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`chunk-label-spaces`](#chunk-label-spaces) | Warning  |

#### Examples

````markdown
```{{r several words}}
1 + 1
```
````

````text
warning: [chunk-label-spaces] Chunk label 'several words' contains spaces and may break Quarto cross-references; use hyphens or underscores
 --> example.qmd:1:7
  |
1 | ```{r several words}
  |       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
````

### `missing-chunk-labels` {#missing-chunk-labels}

Warns about executable code cells with no label. Labels make cells easier to
identify in errors and cross-references.

Add a label in the cell header or in a cell option, such as `#| label: my-plot`.
Use the comment prefix for the cell's language: `#|` for R or Python, `//|` for
C++ or Rust, and `--|` for SQL.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   The Quarto or R Markdown flavor.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                            | Severity |
  | ----------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`missing-chunk-labels`](#missing-chunk-labels) | Warning  |

#### Examples

````markdown
```{{r}}
1 + 1
```
````

````text
warning: [missing-chunk-labels] Executable code chunk has no label; add `#| label: ...`
 --> example.qmd:1:4
  |
1 | ```{r}
  |    ^^^
````

### `quarto-schema` {#quarto-schema}

Warns about YAML values that do not match Quarto's expected type or allowed
choices. It checks frontmatter, code-cell options, and project files such as
`_quarto.yml` and `_metadata.yml`.

Use the expected type or one of the suggested values. Unknown keys are handled
separately by [`quarto-schema-unknown-key`](#quarto-schema-unknown-key).

Set `validate-yaml: false` in the affected document or manifest to skip schema
checks when a filter needs a different form. YAML syntax errors are still
reported. Some deeply nested options and restrictions tied to a particular
output format are not checked.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   The Quarto flavor.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                          | Severity |
  | ---                                                           | ---      |
  | [`quarto-schema-type-mismatch`](#quarto-schema-type-mismatch) | Warning  |
  | [`quarto-schema-invalid-enum`](#quarto-schema-invalid-enum)   | Warning  |

#### `quarto-schema-type-mismatch` {#quarto-schema-type-mismatch}

A value has the wrong type for the option, such as text where a boolean is
required.

#### `quarto-schema-invalid-enum` {#quarto-schema-invalid-enum}

A value is not among the choices allowed for the option.

#### Examples

A boolean option has a text value:

```markdown
---
toc: maybe
---
```

```text
warning: [quarto-schema-type-mismatch] value should be a boolean
 --> example.qmd:2:6
  |
2 | toc: maybe
  |      ^^^^^
```

An option has an unsupported value:

```markdown
---
fig-align: sideways
---
```

```text
warning: [quarto-schema-invalid-enum] invalid value; expected one of: default, left, right, center
 --> example.qmd:2:12
  |
2 | fig-align: sideways
  |            ^^^^^^^^
```

### `quarto-schema-unknown-key` {#quarto-schema-unknown-key}

Warns about unknown or misspelled Quarto options in frontmatter, code-cell
options, and project metadata. Check the suggested spelling or remove the unused
option.

This rule is optional because Quarto allows custom metadata. At the top level,
it warns only about names close to known options. Within sections that permit
only predefined options, it reports any unknown key.

Like [`quarto-schema`](#quarto-schema), it honors `validate-yaml: false`.

Default
:   Off

Enable this rule with `[lint] extend-select = ["quarto-schema-unknown-key"]`.

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   The Quarto flavor.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                      | Severity |
  | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`quarto-schema-unknown-key`](#quarto-schema-unknown-key) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
---
forrmat: html
---
```

```text
warning: [quarto-schema-unknown-key] unknown key `forrmat`; did you mean `format`?
 --> example.qmd:2:1
  |
2 | forrmat: html
  | ^^^^^^^
```

### `figure-crossref-captions` {#figure-crossref-captions}

Warns when a bookdown figure reference, such as `\@ref(fig:plot)`, targets a
code cell without a figure caption. A label alone does not create the figure
that the reference needs.

Add a `fig.cap` or `fig-cap` option to the target cell, or correct the reference
if it points to the wrong cell.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   The Quarto or R Markdown flavor.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                    | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`figure-crossref-captions`](#figure-crossref-captions) | Warning  |

#### Examples

This example uses the R Markdown flavor.

````markdown
Figure \@ref(fig:plot).

```{{r}}
#| label: plot
plot(1:10)
```
````

```text
warning: [figure-crossref-captions] Figure cross-reference '@fig:plot' targets a chunk label without a figure caption (`fig-cap`/`fig.cap`)
 --> example.Rmd:1:14
  |
1 | Figure \@ref(fig:plot).
  |              ^^^^^^^^
```

### `unknown-emoji-alias` {#unknown-emoji-alias}

Warns about emoji shortcodes that Panache does not recognize, such as
`:not-a-real-emoji:`. Check the shortcode's spelling, use a supported alias, or
insert the emoji character directly.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.emoji = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                          | Severity |
  | --------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`unknown-emoji-alias`](#unknown-emoji-alias) | Warning  |

#### Examples

With this configuration:

```toml
[extensions]
emoji = true
```

```markdown
Hello :not-a-real-emoji:
```

```text
warning: [unknown-emoji-alias] Unknown emoji alias ':not-a-real-emoji:'
 --> example.qmd:1:7
  |
1 | Hello :not-a-real-emoji:
  |       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

### `html-entities` {#html-entities}

Warns about misspelled HTML named entities and missing semicolons, such as
`&ellips;` or `&numero`. These may appear literally in rendered text instead of
producing the intended character.

Correct the name and end it with a semicolon, or insert the character directly.
The rule checks prose and skips code, math, raw HTML, and numeric references
such as `&#123;`.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                              | Severity |
  | --------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`html-entities`](#html-entities) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
An ellipsis: &ellips;
```

```text
warning: [html-entities] Unknown HTML entity '&ellips;'
 --> example.qmd:1:14
  |
1 | An ellipsis: &ellips;
  |              ^^^^^^^^
  = help: did you mean '&hellip;'?
```

### `html-unclosed-attribute` {#html-unclosed-attribute}

Warns about an HTML attribute value with an opening quote but no closing quote.
A tag such as `<a id="goal></a>` may appear as ordinary text instead of creating
a link or anchor.

Close the quote at the intended end of the value. Multiline values and unquoted
attributes are allowed. The rule skips code, math, comments, and explicit raw
HTML code spans or fences.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.raw-html = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                  | Severity |
  | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`html-unclosed-attribute`](#html-unclosed-attribute) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
<a id="goal></a>
```

```text
warning: [html-unclosed-attribute] Unclosed quoted value for HTML attribute 'id'
 --> example.qmd:1:7
  |
1 | <a id="goal></a>
  |       ^
  = help: add the matching closing quote at the intended end of the value
```

### `link-text-is-url` {#link-text-is-url}

Warns when a link's visible text exactly repeats its destination URL. The fix
replaces `[https://example.com/](https://example.com/)` with the shorter
autolink `<https://example.com/>`.

Links with a title, formatted text, or any difference between the visible URL
and destination are left alone. This includes differences in trailing slashes.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                    | Severity |
  | --------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`link-text-is-url`](#link-text-is-url) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
[https://example.com/](https://example.com/)
```

```text
warning: [link-text-is-url] Link text is identical to the URL; an autolink is shorter and clearer.
 --> example.qmd:1:1
  |
1 | [https://example.com/](https://example.com/)
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Convert to autolink
  = help: rewrite as `<https://example.com/>`
```

After `panache lint --fix`:

```markdown
<https://example.com/>
```

### `stray-fenced-div-markers` {#stray-fenced-div-markers}

Warns when `:::` or a longer run of colons appears as paragraph text instead of
opening or closing a fenced div. The colons may be misplaced, attached to
another line, or missing an opening fence.

Put each fence on its own line and check that the opening fence has the intended
class or attributes. Wrap literal mentions of `:::` in backticks.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.fenced-divs = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                    | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`stray-fenced-div-markers`](#stray-fenced-div-markers) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
Text with a misplaced ::: marker.
```

```text
warning: [stray-fenced-div-markers] ':::' appears as text, not as a fenced div marker
 --> example.qmd:1:23
  |
1 | Text with a misplaced ::: marker.
  |                       ^^^
  = help: Pandoc only treats ':::' as a fenced div marker when it starts a line on its own (optionally followed by a class or attributes). Add a newline before it, or wrap it in backticks if it's intentional text
```

### `swallowed-list-marker` {#swallowed-list-marker}

Warns when a line that looks like a list item is read as part of the preceding
paragraph. Add a blank line before the list. If the marker is ordinary prose,
escape it, as in `\-`.

Pandoc requires the blank line before a list. CommonMark and GFM allow bullets
and lists starting at `1` to interrupt a paragraph, but a list starting at `2`
still needs separation. The rule reports the first line in a consecutive run of
affected items.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                              | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`swallowed-list-marker`](#swallowed-list-marker) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
Choose one option:
- First choice
- Second choice
```

```text
warning: [swallowed-list-marker] '-' looks like a list marker, but the preceding line pulls it into a paragraph
 --> example.qmd:2:1
  |
2 | - First choice
  | ^
  = note: 2 consecutive lines here start with a list marker; all of them are reflowed into the paragraph above
  = help: Pandoc-markdown never lets a list interrupt a paragraph. Insert a blank line above this line to start a real list, or escape the marker ('\-') if it is meant as prose
```

### `unspaced-list-marker` {#unspaced-list-marker}

Warns about a line containing only `-\` inside a list. The missing space means
it remains part of the current item instead of starting a new item.

Add a space after `-` if you meant a new item, and supply its text. Remove the
marker if you only meant to continue the existing item.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                            | Severity |
  | ----------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`unspaced-list-marker`](#unspaced-list-marker) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
- First item
  -\
- Second item
```

```text
warning: [unspaced-list-marker] Missing whitespace after '-': this line is paragraph text
 --> example.qmd:2:3
  |
2 |   -\
  |   ^^
  = help: If you intended a list item, add a space after '-' and check its indentation. Escape the hyphen as '\-' if it is literal text
```

### `table-column-count` {#table-column-count}

Warns when a pipe table has more cells in a row than its separator row declares.
Pandoc drops the extra cells when rendering the table.

Add the missing columns to the separator row, or remove the extra cells if they
are unintended. Shorter rows are allowed because they are padded with empty
cells.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                        | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`table-column-count`](#table-column-count) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
| a | b | c |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 3 |
```

```text
warning: [table-column-count] This row has 3 cells but the delimiter row declares 2 columns; the 1 extra cell is dropped when the table is rendered
 --> example.qmd:1:11
  |
1 | | a | b | c |
  |           ^
warning: [table-column-count] This row has 3 cells but the delimiter row declares 2 columns; the 1 extra cell is dropped when the table is rendered
 --> example.qmd:3:11
  |
3 | | 1 | 2 | 3 |
  |           ^
```

### `footnote-after-image` {#footnote-after-image}

Warns when a footnote immediately follows a standalone image. Pandoc then treats
the image and note as one paragraph, so the image loses its figure caption.
Figure cross-references may also stop resolving.

Move the footnote inside the caption if it belongs there, or add a blank line
between the image and the note to keep them separate. This check applies when
`extensions.implicit-figures` is enabled.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   `extensions.footnotes = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                            | Severity |
  | ----------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`footnote-after-image`](#footnote-after-image) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
![A caption.](image.png){#fig-plot}
^[A note about the figure.]
```

```text
warning: [footnote-after-image] footnote attached to a standalone image keeps it from becoming a figure
 --> example.qmd:2:1
  |
2 | ^[A note about the figure.]
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = note: an image becomes a figure only when it is alone in its paragraph; the trailing footnote demotes it
  = note: the caption text will render as the image's alt attribute, not as a caption
  = note: the id no longer labels a figure, so cross-references to it will not resolve
  = help: move the footnote inside the caption, as in `![Caption. ^[note]](img.jpg)`, or separate it from the image with a blank line to keep the figure
```

### `footnote-swallowed-by-bracket` {#footnote-swallowed-by-bracket}

Warns when `[` or `(` directly follows an inline footnote's closing bracket.
Pandoc may read the note as a link label instead, leaving the footnote absent
from the output.

The fix inserts a space after the note. For the `(` form it requires
`--unsafe-fixes`: confirm that you intended a footnote rather than a link
preceded by a literal caret.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Requirements
:   `extensions.inline-footnotes = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                              | Severity |
  | ---                                                               | ---      |
  | [`footnote-swallowed-by-bracket`](#footnote-swallowed-by-bracket) | Warning  |

#### Examples

A reference link follows the apparent note:

```markdown
Text^[A note][link].

[link]: https://example.com
```

```text
warning: [footnote-swallowed-by-bracket] Inline footnote is followed directly by a bracket, so pandoc reads the label as a link instead and drops the footnote; insert a space after the closing `]`
 --> example.qmd:1:5
  |
1 | Text^[A note][link].
  |     ^^
  = help: Insert a space after the inline footnote
```

After `panache lint --fix`:

```markdown
Text^[A note] [link].

[link]: https://example.com
```

A parenthesis follows the apparent note:

```markdown
Text^[A note](https://example.com).
```

```text
warning: [footnote-swallowed-by-bracket] Inline footnote is followed directly by a bracket, so pandoc reads the label as a link instead and drops the footnote; insert a space after the closing `]`
 --> example.qmd:1:5
  |
1 | Text^[A note](https://example.com).
  |     ^^
  = help: Insert a space after the inline footnote
```

After `panache lint --fix --unsafe-fixes` (review the change before applying
it):

```markdown
Text^[A note] (https://example.com).
```

### `reversed-footnote-marker` {#reversed-footnote-marker}

Warns about `[^...]` containing prose where an inline footnote may have been
intended. Inline footnotes start with `^[`, as in `^[A note]`.

Confirm the intended meaning before applying the fix, which requires
`--unsafe-fixes`. A valid but undefined label such as `[^missing]` belongs to
[`undefined-references`](#undefined-references). Working links and cases where
swapping the marker would still fail to create a footnote are left unfixed.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Requirements
:   `extensions.inline-footnotes = true`.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                    | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`reversed-footnote-marker`](#reversed-footnote-marker) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
Text [^a longer explanation goes here].
```

```text
warning: [reversed-footnote-marker] Footnote label contains whitespace, so pandoc does not read `[^...]` as a footnote reference; write `^[...]` for an inline footnote
 --> example.qmd:1:6
  |
1 | Text [^a longer explanation goes here].
  |      ^^
  = help: Swap `[^` for the inline-footnote opener `^[`
  = help: the reference form `[^id]` takes a bare label and needs a matching `[^id]:` definition
```

After `panache lint --fix --unsafe-fixes` (review the change before applying
it):

```markdown
Text ^[a longer explanation goes here].
```

### `space-before-punctuation` {#space-before-punctuation}

Warns about spaces or tabs before `.`, `,`, and `;` in paragraph text. The
optional fix removes the gap.

Check the language and intended spacing before applying the fix with
`--unsafe-fixes`. French documents retain spaces before semicolons. The
document's YAML `lang` setting takes precedence over `[format].lang`.

The rule skips code, math, headings, link text, and punctuation sequences such
as `. . .`. The formatter preserves these spaces unless you apply a lint fix.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   Available; see the examples for fix safety.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                    | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`space-before-punctuation`](#space-before-punctuation) | Warning  |

#### Examples

```markdown
We have A   , and B    ; so we have C    .
```

```text
warning: [space-before-punctuation] Space before ',' may be unintended
 --> example.qmd:1:10
  |
1 | We have A   , and B    ; so we have C    .
  |          ^^^
  = help: Remove space before ','
warning: [space-before-punctuation] Space before ';' may be unintended
 --> example.qmd:1:20
  |
1 | We have A   , and B    ; so we have C    .
  |                    ^^^^
  = help: Remove space before ';'
warning: [space-before-punctuation] Space before '.' may be unintended
 --> example.qmd:1:38
  |
1 | We have A   , and B    ; so we have C    .
  |                                      ^^^^
  = help: Remove space before '.'
```

After `panache lint --fix --unsafe-fixes` (review the change before applying
it):

```markdown
We have A, and B; so we have C.
```

### `unsupported-metadata-key` {#unsupported-metadata-key}

Reports YAML frontmatter keys that Pandoc cannot use as metadata. Collection
keys such as `[a, b]: value` and alias keys such as `*name: value` can prevent
the document from rendering.

Replace the key with a normal name, or move the content out of the frontmatter
if it was not meant to be metadata. Scalar keys such as `1` are accepted.
Code-cell options are not checked by this rule.

Default
:   On

Auto-fix
:   No

Requirements
:   The Pandoc, Quarto, or R Markdown flavor.

Diagnostic codes

  | Code                                                    | Severity |
  | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | [`unsupported-metadata-key`](#unsupported-metadata-key) | Error    |

#### Examples

```markdown
---
[a, b]: value
---
```

```text
error: [unsupported-metadata-key] sequence used as a metadata key is not supported by pandoc
 --> example.qmd:2:1
  |
2 | [a, b]: value
  | ^^^^^^
  = note: pandoc converts frontmatter to metadata, where every key must be a string; it fails the whole document with `Non-string keys are not supported`
  = help: quote the key to make it a string, or move the line out of the frontmatter if it was not meant to be metadata
```
